issues.legal_issue: A perpetual dedication to worship at the tomb of an ordinary ancestor is not a valid religious or charitable purpose under Hindu law unless a qualifying religious practice is established.
material_facts: The deed dedicated property for charities and directed that part of the income from property allotted to a matam be spent on puja at a tomb containing the remains of the settlors’ ancestors.
The tomb was not shown to be a shrine associated with a saint or other person whose worship had become a recognized public religious practice.
The person relying on the tomb worship did not plead or prove a community practice of building tombs over ancestors’ remains and performing puja there.
issues.conclusion: The provision for puja at the ancestors’ tomb was invalid as a religious or charitable purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The validity of a religious purpose for a perpetual dedication is determined according to Hindu law and Hindu notions, not English law concerning tombs. A claimed purpose grounded in religious merit must have a Shastric basis, or, if based on a later religious practice, must be shown to have wide recognition among a substantial class. The person asserting such a community practice bears the burden of proving it. An ordinary ancestor’s tomb is not recognized as religious merely because worship is performed there, although the rule may differ for saints or other shrines of recognized public worship, and for certain memorials following cremation. The Court relied on Saraswathi Ammal v. Rajagopal Ammal, Kunhamutty v. Thondikkodan Ahmad Musaliar, A. Drainasundaram Pillai v. N. Subramania Pillai, Veluswami Gounder v. Dandapani, Sri Ramanasramam v. Commissioner for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments, Board of Commissioners for Hindu Religious Endowments v. Pidugu Narasimham, Ratnavelu Mudaliar v. Commissioner for H.R. & C.E., and Ramaswami v. Board of Commissioners. The dispute arose in a suit under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure concerning charitable trusts.

rule.if: charitable_trust_appeal and ancestral_tomb_worship_dedication and ordinary_person_tomb and not community_religious_practice_proved

predicates.charitable_trust_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the validity or administration of a charitable trust.
predicates.ancestral_tomb_worship_dedication: A person has dedicated property to support worship at the tomb of an ancestor.
predicates.ordinary_person_tomb: The tomb is of an ordinary person and is not shown to be a shrine of a saint or another figure of recognized public worship.
predicates.community_religious_practice_proved: The person relying on the dedication has proved that the relevant community widely recognizes the tomb worship as a religious practice.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning a charitable trust involves a dedication for worship at an ordinary ancestor’s tomb and no widely recognized community religious practice is proved, the dedication for tomb worship is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: When property is absolutely endowed to a matam and its income is charged with an invalid purpose, the invalid direction does not defeat the vesting in the matam.
material_facts: The deed expressly dedicated the properties absolutely for the stated charities and said the settlors retained no rights in them.
The relevant schedule described the properties as allotted to the matam.
The deed directed that income from the scheduled properties be used both to feed visitors to the matam and to conduct puja at the attached tomb.
The lower appellate court had divided the properties between the matam charity and the tomb purpose.
issues.conclusion: The properties vested in the matam; the direction to spend income on puja at the tomb was invalid, but the vesting did not fail and the properties were not to be divided between the matam and the tomb purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The deed must be read as a whole to determine whether it transfers the property or merely creates a charge. Here its absolute dedication and relinquishment of the settlors’ rights, read with the schedule allocating the properties to the matam, established vesting in the matam subject to an income direction. The invalid direction for tomb puja did not invalidate that vesting. The Court rejected the High Court’s division of the property and its direction that part go to the trustee. The ruling applied the Court’s construction of the trust deed and its conclusion that the tomb-puja purpose was not valid under Hindu law.

rule.if: charitable_trust_appeal and deed_absolutely_dedicates_property and schedule_allocates_property_to_matam and income_directed_to_tomb_puja

predicates.charitable_trust_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the validity or administration of a charitable trust.
predicates.deed_absolutely_dedicates_property: The deed states that the property is dedicated absolutely and that the donors retain no rights in it.
predicates.schedule_allocates_property_to_matam: The deed’s schedule identifies the matam as the institution to which the property is allotted.
predicates.income_directed_to_tomb_puja: The deed directs that income from the property be spent on worship at an attached tomb.

issues.definition: If a charitable-trust deed absolutely dedicates property, allocates it to a matam, and directs some income to tomb worship, the matam’s vesting survives even though the tomb-puja direction is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: When changed circumstances prevent a charitable trust from carrying out its original feeding purposes as intended, surplus income may be applied as nearly as possible to the donors’ charitable intention.
material_facts: The deed directed feeding of Brahmins visiting the choultry and feeding of agathies and paradesies visiting the matam.
The parties accepted that improved transport had reduced visits to the village and that few people now came to be fed.
The Court directed that, after providing for the beneficiaries who continued to visit, available surplus income could be used to feed poor schoolchildren in the village.
issues.conclusion: The surplus income could be applied to feeding poor schoolchildren, as nearly as possible in accordance with the donors’ charitable intention.
issues.legal_principle: Under the cy-près doctrine, where changed circumstances prevent a charitable purpose from being carried out as the donors intended, the property may be applied to a purpose as nearly as possible to their intention. The Court applied that doctrine to the changed circumstances affecting the original feeding charities.

predicates.charitable_trust_administration_appeal: The proceeding concerns the administration of a charitable trust.
predicates.changed_circumstances_reduce_intended_be: A change in circumstances has substantially reduced the number of people who were intended to receive the charity.
predicates.original_charitable_feeding_purpose_cann: The trustees cannot use all the relevant income for the original feeding purpose as intended because too few intended beneficiaries are available.
predicates.surplus_trust_income_exists: Income remains after providing for the intended beneficiaries who continue to receive the charity.

issues.definition: When changed circumstances prevent a charitable trust from fully carrying out its original feeding purpose and income remains, that income may be used for a charitable purpose close to the donors’ intention.

issues.legal_issue: A court administering a public charitable trust may frame a scheme with a trustee board combining family representation and community representation.
material_facts: The suit sought removal of a trustee for breach of trust and the framing of a scheme for the charities.
The courts below had directed a scheme administered by three trustees, including a member of the donor’s family and two respectable residents of the village.
The Supreme Court agreed that the scheme should have a three-member board with that combination of family and community representation.
issues.conclusion: The scheme should provide for three trustees: one belonging to the donors’ family and two other respectable residents of the community; the subordinate court would appoint them and supervise the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: In the administration of the charitable trusts at issue, the Court approved a scheme with a board combining a member of the donors’ family and community representatives, subject to the subordinate court’s appointment and continuing directions. The judgment does not identify a separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this scheme composition.

predicates.charitable_trust_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-supervised scheme for administering a charitable trust.
predicates.court_orders_scheme_for_trust_administra: The court determines that a scheme should govern the administration of the trust.
predicates.family_and_community_representation_suit: The court considers that the scheme should include both a representative of the donors’ family and representatives of the local community.

issues.definition: When a court orders a scheme for a charitable trust and considers family and community representation suitable, the scheme includes both forms of trustee representation.
